<section class="nv-section">
<h2 class="nv-section-title"><a href="/docs/rules/expressions/conversion-and-intrinsics/">Conversion and the intrinsics</a><span class="nv-section-count">8</span></h2>
<p class="nv-section-blurb">The failable conversion that answers null instead of throwing, and what the compiler prepares from a literal argument.</p>
<ol class="nv-rule-list"><li><a href="/docs/rules/expressions/conversion-and-intrinsics/#intrinsic-literals">A literal argument to an intrinsic <code>Core</code> call is validated while checking and prepared into the artifact</a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="shipped">Shipped</span><span class="nv-rule-list-flag" title="Differs from PHP">PHP</span></li><li><a href="/docs/rules/expressions/conversion-and-intrinsics/#intrinsic-list-is-closed">The intrinsic roster is a closed set in the compiler's own source, and nothing declares itself into it</a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="shipped">Shipped</span></li><li><a href="/docs/rules/expressions/conversion-and-intrinsics/#bracket-destructuring"><code>list(...)</code> does not parse; <code>[...]</code> is the only destructuring target</a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="shipped">Shipped</span><span class="nv-rule-list-flag" title="Differs from PHP">PHP</span></li><li><a href="/docs/rules/expressions/conversion-and-intrinsics/#nullable-conversion"><code>expr as ?T</code> yields the converted value or <code>null</code>, and never throws</a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="shipped">Shipped</span><span class="nv-rule-list-flag" title="Differs from PHP">PHP</span></li><li><a href="/docs/rules/expressions/conversion-and-intrinsics/#nullable-conversion-availability"><code>as ?T</code> is refused where the conversion cannot fail, where none exists, and at every class target</a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="shipped">Shipped</span><span class="nv-rule-list-flag" title="Differs from PHP">PHP</span></li><li><a href="/docs/rules/expressions/conversion-and-intrinsics/#conversion-keeps-qualifiers"><code>as ?T</code> decides <code>tainted</code> and <code>secret</code> by exactly the rule <code>as T</code> uses, and launders nothing of its own</a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="shipped">Shipped</span></li><li><a href="/docs/rules/expressions/conversion-and-intrinsics/#try-parse">A failable single-<code>string</code> parse is spelled <code>tryParse</code>, and no separate validity predicate stands beside it</a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="shipped">Shipped</span><span class="nv-rule-list-flag" title="Differs from PHP">PHP</span></li><li><a href="/docs/rules/expressions/conversion-and-intrinsics/#preparation-preserves-behaviour">The prepared path and the runtime path are one implementation, so preparation is only earlier and never different</a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="shipped">Shipped</span></li></ol>
